memory: I am learning how AI agents work, especially tool calling, agent loops, state, context, and memory.
I am building a research agent in Python using Gemini and Tavily.
I am learning RAG and want to understand retrieval mechanisms deeply rather than only using frameworks.
I have previously implemented RAG using vector search and ChromaDB.
I am currently learning how long-term memory differs from conversation history and model context.
I prefer concise technical explanations with practical examples.
I am a student and I am focused on developing strong computer science fundamentals.
I am learning about embeddings and how text can be represented as vectors.
I want to understand cosine similarity and how it is used to compare embeddings.
I am currently implementing vector-based retrieval for the memory system in my research agent.
After vector retrieval, I plan to learn hybrid retrieval that combines lexical and semantic search.
After understanding hybrid retrieval, I plan to learn reranking as a second-stage retrieval mechanism.
I want to understand the failure modes and trade-offs of different retrieval methods.
I prefer implementing concepts manually before using frameworks that abstract away the underlying mechanisms.
Eventually I want to understand LangGraph as an abstraction over agent state, nodes, transitions, and control flow.
I am learning agent architecture progressively rather than trying to build a production-ready agent immediately.
I want to understand why an agent chooses a particular tool and how tool results influence later decisions.
I am interested in understanding how memory retrieval decides which stored information should enter the model context.
I am currently using a persistent JSON file as the storage layer for long-term memory.
I want to compare naive retrieval, lexical retrieval, vector retrieval, hybrid retrieval, and reranking.
